$comment: Benchmark target list — LABELS (tracked, fallback run list for a fresh clone). target-1..target-4 are aliases, nothing more: each label is the committed directory name under benchmark/results/<label>/, and the label -> repo mapping is published openly in benchmark/targets.json (label_map) and benchmark/README.md, "Target anonymity". run.mjs reads benchmark/repos.local.json when it exists (the author's 21-repo list) and falls back to this file, so a fresh clone runs these five shipped-run targets. Every url and commit below was copied from the committed evidence — url from benchmark/targets.json, commit from benchmark/results/<label>/meta.json (field "commit", written by benchmark/run.mjs from git rev-parse HEAD) — never typed from memory. NOTE: run.mjs does not check out the recorded commit; it shallow-clones the default branch and re-resolves HEAD, recording that resolved commit in results/<name>/meta.json. To reproduce a shipped run at its pinned commit, clone and then check out the commit listed here. realworld-control is a real name, not a label, because it is already public via examples/realworld-assessment — the control must be independently reproducible, and naming it leaks nothing that is not already in the repo. SAMPLING LIMITATION, stated up front: two of the four labelled targets are by the same author and share a Next.js house style, and three of four are TypeScript. This is a small, convenience sample, not a representative one. The mapping real-name -> label is defined ONCE in benchmark/anonymize-results.mjs (LABEL_MAP) — a tracked file, so the mapping was never actually withheld; publishing it in targets.json costs no anonymity and makes the sample verifiable. See benchmark/README.md, "Target anonymity".

targets.provenance: Reference implementation (NestJS + Prisma + JWT). Control, not a vibe-coding sample.
